questions.question: Which field does a switch use to associate an incoming port with a station?
questions.explanation: A source MAC provides evidence that the station is reachable via the ingress port.

questions.question: What does an IPv4 host learn from a successful ARP exchange for an on-link peer?
questions.explanation: ARP resolves an on-link IPv4 address to a link-layer address.

questions.question: A switch receives a unicast frame whose destination MAC is absent from the table. What happens under ordinary forwarding?

options.A: Flood every VLAN on the switch
options.B: Send it back out the incoming port only
options.C: Flood out other forwarding ports in the same VLAN
options.D: Drop it until it receives an ARP reply

questions.explanation: Unknown unicast flooding is scoped to the frame's VLAN and excludes ingress.

questions.question: A frame enters Gi1/0/1. The entry for its destination in the same VLAN points to Gi1/0/8. Which action follows?

options.C: Drop because the source port differs

questions.explanation: Known unicast is forwarded to the port associated with the destination MAC.

questions.question: A frame arrives on Gi1/0/9 and its destination MAC is already learned on Gi1/0/9. What does the switch do?

options.A: Flood it on all other ports
options.B: Filter it instead of sending it back out Gi1/0/9
options.C: Send it back to the same port
options.D: Replace the destination MAC and forward

questions.explanation: The destination is on the ingress segment, so no forwarding to another port is needed.

questions.question: What happens to an idle dynamic MAC-table entry after its aging interval expires?

options.A: It is removed and may be learned again on subsequent traffic
options.D: Its VLAN membership changes to the native VLAN

questions.explanation: Dynamic forwarding associations age out when no qualifying source traffic refreshes them.

questions.question: Which Catalyst IOS command clears dynamic MAC-table entries without removing the maintained device configuration?
questions.explanation: Dynamic forwarding entries are held independently of both ARP and the startup configuration.

questions.question: A workstation has no cached neighbor entry and sends traffic to a remote subnet through 192.0.2.1. Which IPv4 address appears as its ARP target?
questions.explanation: The gateway is the Ethernet next hop. The remote address remains the IP packet's destination.

questions.question: A host moves to another switch port in the same VLAN. What updates its dynamic forwarding entry before the old entry ages out?

options.A: A ping to another VLAN using some other host's MAC
options.B: A read of the current ARP table
options.C: A source frame from its MAC on the new port
options.D: A destination frame sent to its MAC on the old port

questions.explanation: Ordinary source learning updates the association when the switch sees the MAC on its new port.

questions.question: Two IPv4 hosts share a LAN. ARP resolves the neighbor correctly, but an engineer needs the physical switch port for that MAC. Which table supplies it?
questions.explanation: ARP supplies the IP-to-MAC relation. The switch table supplies the VLAN and port for a learned MAC.
